points.label: Action and response
points.left: David comes alone to Ahimelech, gives a mission account, receives consecrated bread, and asks for the sword kept behind the ephod.
points.right: David flees to Gath, hears the servants identify him through the victory song, becomes afraid, and changes his behavior before the king.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places flight acquires food, a weapon, and a dangerous witness inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the celebrated warrior survives by appearing mad inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: 1 Samuel 21:1–9 and 1 Samuel 21:10–15 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Flight, Covenant, and Restraint” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.
payload.tension: 1 Samuel 21:1–9 foregrounds flight acquires food, a weapon, and a dangerous witness; 1 Samuel 21:10–15 foregrounds the celebrated warrior survives by appearing mad. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
payload.title: Holy bread and Goliath’s sword / David disguises himself before Achish
